messages:
maya: quick follow-up on the package/upgrade RFC — idea: before applying any delta in air-gapped installs, run a package-graph consistency interlock. validate the full DAG of artifacts and require short-lived leases per node so we avoid overlapping incompatible changes.

kevin: sketch the model? central lock server or gossip between agents?

maya: hybrid. control-plane issues leases when reachable. agents have a fallback handshake: exchange signed preflight receipts with peers and refuse apply unless required receipts present.

david: signatures & PKI are a pain for customers in airgap. can we make this optional?

maya: yes. signature required in high-trust mode. optional in low-trust. use verifier-agent keys (we already surface KMS/HSM in Private).

kevin: what about nodes that are offline for days? we can't block forever in many deployments.

maya: propose two modes: strict (block if peer missing) and best-effort (warn + allow after N days with operator override). receipts carry a validity window and an offline policy flag.

sara: operator override must be audited. require a one-time signed override key and write an offline audit record. no silent drift.

maya: agreed. here's a tiny proto sketch for the handshake (min payloads):

```
service Interlock {
  rpc RequestLease(LeaseRequest) returns (LeaseResponse);
  rpc ExchangeReceipt(Receipt) returns (ReceiptAck);
}

message LeaseRequest { string node = 1; string target_manifest = 2; }
message LeaseResponse { string lease_id = 1; int64 expires_unix = 2; }
message Receipt { string node = 1; string lease_id = 2; bytes signature = 3; string root_manifest = 4; }
```

kevin: receipts are small enough to transfer over USB? keep them minimal, reference content-addressed blobs for everything else.

maya: yes — receipts reference manifest hashes rather than bundling artifacts. that keeps sneakernet friendly.

david: avoid global locks. make leases scoped to component groups (storage, runtime, model-weights). use compatibility constraints on edges for cross-group checks.

maya: nodes schema idea: id, artifact_hash, compatibility_tags, drain_hooks, preflight_script_refs. edges have constraints like required-runtime>=X or drain-before-upgrade=true.

kevin: drain hooks increase ops complexity. ship safe defaults (no-op) plus curated hooks for common services (PG, Redis, ingress). let customers opt-in advanced hooks.

maya: interlock should be a single pluggable interface: validateGraph + signReceipt. verifier only needs to implement those.

arch-review-bot: note: must integrate with content-addressed bundles + manifest chaining from earlier RFC. receipts should include root manifest hash to allow offline proof verification.

sara: rollback question: if an apply fails mid-graph, who leads recovery? agents or coordinator?

maya: agents should be conservative: if an apply fails, report and hold the lease until operator picks rollback vs retry. coordinator can compute suggested rollforward/rollback sequences but final action is operator-driven.

kevin: lease lifetimes matter. default 5m, with agent automatic extensions + exponential backoff and operator ability to extend for long jobs. avoid long blocking windows by design.

maya: also require append-only audit for lease create/extend/expire signed by agent key. store locally and surface in console.

maya: propose a preflight dry-run that outputs: compatibility report, affected services, estimated downtime windows. run this during CI for on-prem bundles.

david: bootstrap trust path for first install?

maya: bootstrap flow: operator signs initial root manifest offline; installer imports root key into local keystore (HSM optional); subsequent receipts chain to root manifest. include a simple quickstart for this.

kevin: documentation burden is real. ship a quickstart + UI for manual override and audit retrieval.

sara: consider passive mode: interlock runs and reports drift but never blocks (customers can opt into full blocking later).

maya: will include passive vs blocking mode in the draft. also add compatibility matrix for drain-before-upgrade patterns and recommended default hooks.

arch-review-bot: request: write a short RFC follow-up outlining API sketch, offline bootstrap, lease semantics, failure modes, and compatibility matrix for drain patterns.

maya: i'll draft and ping eng-runtime + eng-onprem. ops-bot: can you schedule a 30m sync this week?

ops-bot: scheduled "Interlock sync" Thu 11:00am PST. Invitees: maya, david, kevin, sara, eng-runtime, eng-onprem

kevin: last thought — passive monitoring mode + gradual adoption path is important. thanks all :thumbsup:
